datasheet.title: Celestica DS4001 1U 32-port 400GbE Data Center Switch datasheet

description: Celestica DS4001 1U 32-port 400GbE data center switch - 32 QSFP-DD in two belly-to-belly rows of sixteen (ports 1, 2, 31 and 32 printed '-HP', the 20 W high-power positions), a stacked pair of 10G SFP+ management ports (M1/M2) at the LEFT end, and at the right four status lamps and a vertical console RJ45 / USB-A / management RJ45 stack; at the rear two 1500 W supplies (1+1) either side of seven hot-swap fans (6+1). 12.8 Tbps, 70 MB buffer. The DS4000 shares its installation guide and rear but has a different faceplate.

gaps.note: The docs-portal What's in the Box lists R3240-F9104-A1, '1U,32X400GBE,DC PSU 2x1500W,COMe 4C/16G DDR4/64G SSD,F2B', and the Ground Lug Installation page exists because a DC build does ('The GLA is not applicable to the AC SKU versions'). The PDF revision 1.4.0 of the same guide lists only the two AC SKUs, and no held image shows the DC supply's face, so no DC supply component or configuration is drawn.

name: ds4001

chassis.note: datasheet - height 43.1 mm (1.73 in, 1 EIA unit), width 438.5 mm (17.3 in), depth 657.5 mm (25.8 in); the guide's specifications table agrees. No weight stated in any held document.

colour.note: render - black face, white legends, silver cage bezels and jack plate; light grey sheet metal. So chassis.color is the sheet metal (#c4c8cc, which the top, bottom, sides and the rear frame between the modules wear - the rear webs are grey in the guide CAD and silver in the DS4001 rear render), and the black front bezel is a full-face decor rect under everything else on the front, since a view carries no colour of its own.

environment.note: datasheet 'Temperature: 0 C to 45 C @ 900m, Humidity: 5% to 90%, non-condensing'; the shared guide's table says 5 - 40 C for either airflow and 40 - 60 % operating humidity, 5 - 95 % storage. Both carried, as on the DS4000.

front-geometry.note: THE FRONT IS FROM A PERSPECTIVE RENDER, MEASURED THROUGH A ONE-DIMENSIONAL HOMOGRAPHY. On ds4001_front.png the face recedes to the left, so no scale can be taken straight off it (a straight-line fit of the sixteen column centres leaves 16.2 px rms). Positions along the face were measured on FLAT features only - the white port-lamp dots, which sit on the face plane, not the cage bezels, which stand proud: each column's upper-left and upper-right dot pair was located by connected-component search in the black face and its midpoint taken as the column centre. A projective map x = (a i + b)/(c i + 1) over column index i fits those sixteen centres to 0.10 px rms. Mapping the face's two outer edges through it gives a face 19.147 pitches wide, so the pitch is 438.5 / 19.147 = 22.902 mm - against 22.894 measured square-on on the DS4000's orthographic guide elevation, 0.03 percent apart. That agreement is the check: a wrong geometry does not reproduce the sibling's pitch from the face width. With the DS4000 pitch: column 1 centre 39.19 mm from the left edge (the DS4000's is 24.33, so the whole QSFP-DD block sits 14.86 mm further right, making room for the SFP+ pair); SFP+ lamp 16.93, so SFP+ centre 20.06 using the DS4000's lamp-to-cage offset (3.13 mm; the protruding cage's own blob centroid gives 20.1-21.1, biased right by its visible side wall); status lamps 400.4; management plate 403.6-420.65; lug tag centred 427.3. Image x was corrected for the face's vertical lean (0.0625 px per px, from the left edge at two heights) before mapping features measured off the dot line. Vertical positions are NOT measured on the render; they are carried from the DS4000's orthographic elevation (same cages on the same pitch), which is recorded as borrowed.

front-vertical.note: borrowed from celestica/ds4000's qsfp-layout, port-leds, sfp-and-status and mgmt provenance (guide front elevation, y as a fraction of 43.1 mm): QSFP-DD openings at y 9.36 (top row) and 22.97 (bottom), lamp windows at 4.54/7.26 and 35.16/37.85, SFP+ cages at 9.45 and 22.9, SFP+ lamps at 6.73 and 35.8, status lamps from 11.9 on 5.0 mm, management plate 6.73-38.63. The render agrees with this ordering and with the lamps being above and below the SFP+ pair, but is not measured for it.

legends.note: read off ds4001_front at 3x: '1-HP up-down 2-HP', '3 up-down 4' ... '29 up-down 30', '31-HP up-down 32-HP' between the rows, solid triangles; 'M1 up-down M2' between the SFP+ cages; 'STAT', 'FAN', 'PWR', 'ALM' set diagonally left of the four lamps; 'IOIOI', a USB trident and a network symbol to the right of the jacks; 'Celestica' set in plain type above the jacks (a wordmark in text, not a logo); 'DS4001' along the lug tag. The -HP ports are the guide's high-power positions (QSFP-DD Port Power Outputs: F2B 20 W on ports 1, 2, 31 and 32).

lifecycle.note: searched 2026-09-26 for a DS4000/DS4001 end-of-life or end-of-sale announcement; none found.

mgmt.note: render - a silver plate holding, top to bottom, an RJ45 with its keyway UP (console, IOIOI), a USB-A, and an RJ45 with its keyway DOWN and two lamp windows in its lower corners (management, network symbol) - the DS4000's arrangement. Jack cells std/rj45-ganged@2 as on the DS4000. The USB is USB 2.0 (datasheet), so std/usb-a@1 is seated with its usb2 skin.

model-split.note: The guide's three front elevations are the DS4000's faceplate (SFP+ at the right, beside the lamps; see celestica/ds4000). Every DS4001 image held - its datasheet render, the Foleon ds4001_front render and the Foleon side-by-side - shows a different faceplate: the SFP+ pair at the LEFT end with a green lamp above and below it, legends 'M1 up-down M2', '1-HP up-down 2-HP' and '31-HP up-down 32-HP', a hexagon-perforated black face, and the lug tag printed 'DS4001'. So this front is modelled from the renders and carries no guide front figure at all.

port-leds.note: The render shows the same arrangement the guide's QSFP-DD Port LED Locations page draws - two lamps stacked at the upper left and two at the upper right of each top-row cage, the same below each bottom-row cage - and the dot-pair spacing is 0.70 of the column pitch on the render (e.g. 80.0 of 115.5 px at column 4) against 0.70 on the DS4000 elevation (55.65 of 79.67 px), so the DS4000's +/-8.0 mm is used. Four tri-colour lamps per port per the guide; lower-port lamp numbering follows the upper port's reading order (inference, as on the DS4000). THE -HP COLUMNS DIFFER, AND THIS IS A READING, NOT A GUESS: at 5x on the native render, columns 1 and 16 (ports 1, 2, 31, 32) show ONE white window at each side above the top cage and one at each side below the bottom cage, where every other column shows a stacked pair; on the rectified render they sit at column centre -11.3 and +11.3 mm, y 5.8 and 36.4, outside the cage bezel. The -HP cages are also drawn flush where the others stand proud with spring fingers - a different cage. So those four ports carry two lamp windows each here (ids -1 left, -2 right), against the guide's general 'four tri-color LEDs' per port, which its own close-up shows on the DS4000's port 31; see the hp-port-lamps gap.

port-power.note: guide, QSFP-DD Port Power Outputs (shared) - F2B 28 x 15 W + 4 x 20 W (ports 1, 2, 31, 32); B2F 24 x 5 W + 8 x 12 W (ports 25-32). DS4001 datasheet: 'Up to 12W in Back to Front airflow', 'Up to 20W in Front to Back airflow'.

power.note: datasheet - '1+1 redundant, hot swap PSUs, 1500W each'; 'AC 47~63Hz, 100 ~ 240 V nominal, 90~264V max'. Unlike the DS4000's, the DS4001 datasheet states no system consumption figure, so no power-max-w is carried. The guide's What's in the Box (docs-portal HTML) lists a DC build, R3240-F9104-A1 'DC PSU 2x1500W', which the PDF revision 1.4.0 no longer lists; no DC supply is drawn anywhere held, so it is a gap, not a configuration.

rear.note: the shared guide's Figure 4 rear elevation, measured exactly as recorded on celestica/ds4000 (3.8404 px/mm across, 3.898 down): ground strip with an earth symbol and two screws at the left, PSU2, seven fans on 43.96 mm with FAN7 leftmost, PSU1 at the right. The DS4001 rear render (Foleon ds4001-side-by-side) agrees in every count and arrangement and supplies the colours: black fans with blue latches, silver supplies with black U-handles and orange latches. Positions are the guide figure's, not the render's.

sources.note: DS4001 datasheet (cls_datasheet_DS4001.pdf, 2 pp) for dimensions, interfaces, power, cooling, environment, approvals and ordering lines; the shared DS4000/DS4001 Installation Guide (docs portal pages staged in the intake, and the 49-page PDF rev 1.4.0, 2/2026) for the specifications table, the rear elevation (Product Overview Figure 4), the LED tables, the QSFP-DD LED locations and power classes, and What's in the Box; and the vendor's product renders for the FRONT - the Foleon page's ds4001_front.png (3840 x 1688, three-quarter view, pull tab printed 'DS4001'), the DS4001 datasheet's embedded render (992 x 603) and the Foleon ds4001-side-by-side (front and rear). No photograph of a real unit is held.

vents.note: The render's face is perforated with hexagonal cells - a column at each end, and a cluster between each column's lamp pairs above and below the cages. Drawn with the library's hexagon vent pattern over a backing plate (left x 0.8-9.4, right 430.4-437.6, and an 11.6 x 5.4 patch per column above and below) - the right area and cell shape, the cell count and exact outline estimated.

views.note: TOP (y = 0 at the rear), BOTTOM, LEFT (x = 0 rear) and RIGHT (x = 0 front) as on celestica/ds4000 - the DS4001 renders show the same lid (two perforated fields at the side edges, perforated strips along the front third of each side edge, a recessed lid-release plate on the centreline in the rear third), positions estimated from the renders; side rail fasteners at estimated positions.

placements.description: guide Table 1 Front Panel Status LEDs, System row (sign SYS in the table, STAT on the artwork) - Green/Amber alternate blinking (normal operation), Off (no power to system)
guide Table 1, Fan row - Green On (all fans operating normally), Amber On (one or more fans absent or operating abnormally), Off (no power to system)

guide Table 1, Power Supply Unit row (sign PSU in the table, PWR on the artwork) - Green On (all PSUs operating normally), Amber On (one or more PSUs absent or operating abnormally), Off (no power to system)
guide Table 1, Alarm row - Green On (no alarm), Amber On (critical alarm), Amber 1Hz blinking (minor alarm), Amber 4Hz blinking (major alarm)

guide Table 3 Port Indicator Lights - Ethernet port active (left): Green on (link at 1000Mbps), Amber on (link in 10/100Mbps), Off (link down); Ethernet port active (right): Green blinking (link active with traffic), Off (no traffic)
